title: Tezkor nutqdagi ohang va niyatni ilg‘ash
goal_uz: Dars oxirida tez va tabiiy ingliz nutqida so‘zlovchining aytilmagan niyatini, munosabatini va kinoyasini aniqlaysiz, munosabat belgilari va ohangni farqlaysiz, qisqargan shakllarni to‘liq shaklga keltirasiz va besh qisqa parchadan kamida to‘rttasida so‘zlovchi maqsadini to‘g‘ri topasiz.

scenes.title: Ohang va niyat
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time we dissected a band nine essay. Today we listen between the lines: what people mean, how they feel, and when they are joking.
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum, xush kelibsiz! Oldingi darsda 9 ballik esseni gapma-gap tahlil qildik va matnni tizimli tekshirishni o‘rgandik. Bugun yozuvdan tinglashga o‘tamiz, lekin oddiy tinglashga emas. Dars oxirida tez nutqda so‘zlovchi aslida nima demoqchi ekanini, uning munosabatini va hazil yoki kinoyasini ilg‘aysiz.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. Oldingi safar 9 ballik esseni tahlil qildik. Bugun satrlar orasini tinglaymiz: odamlar nimani nazarda tutadi, nimani his qiladi va qachon hazillashadi.

scenes.title: So‘z va niyat
board: What is said ≠ what is meant
scenes.say: Speakers imply; listeners infer. At this level, the words are rarely the problem. The challenge is working out why someone chose those words, in that tone, at that moment.
scenes.say_native: C2 darajasida tinglashning eng qiyin qismi so‘zlarni emas, niyatni tushunish. So‘zlovchi ishora qiladi, inglizcha “imply”, tinglovchi esa xulosa chiqaradi, ya’ni “infer”. Bu ikki fe’lni adashtirmang: “imply” so‘zlovchining, “infer” tinglovchining ishi. Bugun to‘rt narsani o‘rganamiz: yashirin ma’no, munosabat belgilari, hazil va kinoya hamda tez nutq xususiyatlari.
scenes.say_uz: So‘zlovchi ishora qiladi, tinglovchi xulosa chiqaradi. Bu darajada so‘zlar kamdan-kam muammo bo‘ladi. Qiyini, nega aynan shu so‘zlar, shu ohangda, shu paytda tanlanganini tushunish.

scenes.title: Bilvosita javob
board: B: I’ve been in meetings all day. (= No)
A: Fancy a coffee? B: I’ve got a deadline at five. (= No)
scenes.say: When an answer seems unrelated to the question, it is almost never random. The speaker expects you to fill the gap: I have been in meetings all day means no, and here is my excuse.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi mavzu: yashirin ma’no. Ko‘pincha javob savolga to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri mos kelmaydi, lekin tinglovchi baribir tushunadi. “Hisobot tayyormi?” degan savolga “Kun bo‘yi majlisda bo‘ldim” javobi aslida “yo‘q” va uzr. Tinglovchi shunday mantiq yuritadi: javob bir sababga ko‘ra aytildi, demak, uning ortida ma’no bor. Inglizlar ayniqsa rad javobini shunday bilvosita beradi.
scenes.say_uz: Javob savolga aloqasiz ko‘rinsa, bu deyarli hech qachon tasodif emas. So‘zlovchi bo‘shliqni to‘ldirishingizni kutadi: kun bo‘yi majlisda bo‘ldim degani yo‘q, mana uzrim degani.

scenes.title: Britancha muloyimlik kodi
board: I hear what you say. (= I disagree)
That’s an interesting idea. (= I’m not convinced)
I’ll bear it in mind. (= probably not)
With the greatest respect… (= you’re wrong)
scenes.say: With the greatest respect is rarely respectful. It usually signals that the speaker is about to tell you, very politely, that you are completely wrong.
scenes.say_native: Britaniya ingliz tilida, ayniqsa ish muhitida, muloyim iboralar ko‘pincha teskari ma’noni yashiradi. “I hear what you say” odatda “men qo‘shilmayman” degani. “That’s an interesting idea” ko‘pincha shubhani bildiradi. “I’ll bear it in mind” ko‘p hollarda “bunga qaytmayman”. “With the greatest respect” esa deyarli har doim keskin e’tiroz oldidan keladi. Albatta, kontekst hal qiladi.
scenes.say_uz: With the greatest respect kamdan-kam hurmat bildiradi. Odatda u so‘zlovchi sizga juda muloyim tarzda butunlay noto‘g‘ri ekaningizni aytmoqchi ekanini bildiradi.

scenes.title: O‘zbek tili bilan qiyos
board: English: I’ll see what I can do.
scenes.say: You already decode indirectness every day in Uzbek. The skill transfers; only the signals change. I will see what I can do often means much the same as ko‘ramiz.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek madaniyati ham bilvosita gapirishga moyil. “Ko‘ramiz”, “Bir gap bo‘lar” yoki “Xudo xohlasa” ko‘pincha aniq “ha” emas. Demak, bilvosita nutq sizga tanish. Muammo boshqa joyda: o‘zbek o‘quvchisi ingliz tilini darslikdan o‘rgangani uchun inglizcha iboralarni so‘zma-so‘z qabul qiladi. Ona tilida o‘zingiz osongina ilg‘aydigan ishoralarni inglizchada ham qidirishni o‘rganing.
scenes.say_uz: Siz o‘zbek tilida bilvosita nutqni har kuni tushunasiz. Ko‘nikma o‘tadi, faqat ishoralar o‘zgaradi. I will see what I can do ko‘pincha ko‘ramiz bilan deyarli bir ma’noda.

scenes.title: So‘zma-so‘z tushunish
scenes.say: In British English, quite good is usually a modest compliment, and with a doubtful tone it can sound distinctly unimpressed. In American English, quite tends to mean very.
scenes.say_native: Ikki keng tarqalgan xato. Birinchisi, “I’ll think about it” yoki “I’ll bear it in mind” ni rozilik deb qabul qilish. Ko‘pincha bu muloyim rad. Ikkinchisi, “quite”. Britaniya ingliz tilida urg‘usiz “quite good” odatda “anchagina yaxshi, lekin a’lo emas” degani. Amerika ingliz tilida esa “quite” ko‘pincha “juda” ma’nosida. Kim gapirayotganiga qarab xulosa qiling.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniya ingliz tilida quite good odatda kamtarona maqtov, shubhali ohang bilan esa aniq norozilik bo‘lib eshitiladi. Amerika ingliz tilida quite ko‘pincha juda degani.

scenes.title: Aslida nima demoqchi?
board: 1 A: Can you come on Saturday? B: It’s my sister’s wedding.
2 A: Did you like my presentation? B: The slides were very colourful.
3 A: Shall we hire him? B: I hear what you’re saying.
4 A: Is the restaurant good? B: Well, it’s cheap.
scenes.say: One: Can you come on Saturday? It’s my sister’s wedding. Two: Did you like my presentation? The slides were very colourful. Three: Shall we hire him? I hear what you’re saying. Four: Is the restaurant good? Well, it’s cheap.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta qisqa suhbat. Har birida B aslida nima demoqchi ekanini aniqlang: rozimi, rad etyaptimi, tanqid qilyaptimi? Javob qaysi narsani tilga olmaganiga ham e’tibor bering: maqtalmagan narsa ko‘pincha eng muhim ishora. Har biriga bir gaplik izoh bering.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Shanba kuni kela olasanmi? Singlimning to‘yi. Ikki: Taqdimotim yoqdimi? Slaydlar juda rang-barang edi. Uch: Uni ishga olamizmi? Gapingizni eshityapman. To‘rt: Restoran yaxshimi? Xo‘sh, arzon.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 4 Not really — the only merit is price.
scenes.say: In two and four, the key was what B chose not to praise. Silence about the main point is often the loudest signal in English conversation.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: kela olmayman, sababi to‘y. Ikkinchi: slaydlar maqtaldi, mazmun esa yo‘q, demak, mazmun zaif edi. Uchinchi: “I hear what you’re saying” bu yerda qo‘shilmaslik. To‘rtinchi: “Well” va faqat arzonlikni tilga olish restoran unchalik yaxshi emasligini bildiradi. Ikkinchi va to‘rtinchida asosiy ishora aytilmagan narsada edi.
scenes.say_uz: Ikkinchi va to‘rtinchida kalit B maqtamagan narsada edi. Asosiy narsa haqida jim turish ingliz suhbatida ko‘pincha eng kuchli ishora.

scenes.title: Munosabat belgilari

examples.t: Actually, I think it’s on Tuesday.
To be honest, I found it a bit slow.
examples.uz: Rostini aytsam, menga biroz zerikarli tuyuldi.

scenes.say: Discourse markers are signposts. When you hear to be honest, brace yourself for criticism; when you hear to be fair, expect the speaker to soften a previous complaint.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu: munosabat belgilari. Bu kichik so‘zlar keyingi gapni oldindan e’lon qiladi. “Well” gap boshida ko‘pincha ikkilanish yoki yumshoq e’tirozni bildiradi. “Actually” oldingi fikrni to‘g‘rilaydi. “To be fair” qarshi tomonga yon beradi. “Frankly” yoki “To be honest” eshitilsa, tanqidga tayyorlaning. Tez nutqda bu belgilar sizning yo‘l ko‘rsatkichlaringiz.
scenes.say_uz: Munosabat belgilari yo‘l ko‘rsatkichlari. To be honest eshitsangiz, tanqidga tayyorlaning; to be fair eshitsangiz, so‘zlovchi oldingi shikoyatini yumshatishini kuting.

scenes.title: Munosabat ravishlari

examples.t: It was supposedly the best hotel in town.
examples.uz: Go‘yo u shahardagi eng yaxshi mehmonxona edi.

scenes.say: Notice how one adverb changes the speaker’s position. It was the best hotel in town is a fact. It was supposedly the best hotel in town tells you the speaker was disappointed.
scenes.say_native: Ravishlar ham munosabatni bildiradi. “Apparently” eshitilgan, lekin tekshirilmagan ma’lumot. “Supposedly” undan kuchliroq shubha: “go‘yo”. “Surely” savolda hayrat yoki ishonmaslikni bildiradi: “Surely you’re not leaving?” “nahotki ketyapsiz”. “Admittedly” esa zaif tomonni tan oladi. Bitta ravish butun gapning ohangini o‘zgartiradi.
scenes.say_uz: Bitta ravish so‘zlovchi pozitsiyasini qanday o‘zgartirishiga e’tibor bering. U shahardagi eng yaxshi mehmonxona edi, bu fakt. Go‘yo eng yaxshisi edi, desa, so‘zlovchi hafsalasi pir bo‘lganini bildiradi.

scenes.title: Ohang: tushish va ko‘tarilish
scenes.say: The fall-rise is the most useful tone to recognise. When someone says the food was good with a fall and then a rise, they are inviting you to hear the unspoken but.
scenes.say_native: Ohang ham ma’no tashiydi. Pasayuvchi ohang ishonch va yakunni bildiradi. Pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang esa aytilmagan “lekin” ni bildiradi: “The food was good ↘↗” deyilsa, “lekin boshqa narsa yomon edi” degan ishora bor. Kuchli tushish his-hayajonni ko‘rsatadi. Tekis, jonsiz ohang zerikish yoki jiddiy yuz bilan aytilgan kinoyani bildirishi mumkin.
scenes.say_uz: Pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohangni tanish eng foydali. Kimdir ovqat yaxshi edi deb, ohangni tushirib, keyin ko‘tarsa, sizni aytilmagan lekin ni eshitishga taklif qiladi.

scenes.title: O‘zbek yuklamalari bilan qiyos
scenes.say: Uzbek packs attitude into tiny particles. English spreads it across intonation and short words, so you have to listen to the music of the sentence, not just its grammar.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida munosabatni ko‘pincha yuklamalar tashiydi: “Bugun shanba-ku!”, “Kelgan edim-da”, “Sen-chi?”. Bitta “-ku” e’tiroz va hayratni birdan bildiradi. Ingliz tilida bunday qo‘shimcha yo‘q, shuning uchun bu vazifani ohang, “surely”, “actually”, “but” va gap tuzilishi bajaradi. “Bugun shanba-ku” inglizchada “But it’s Saturday!” ohang bilan aytiladi. Yuklamani qidirmang, ohangni tinglang.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbek tili munosabatni kichik yuklamalarga joylaydi. Ingliz tili uni ohang va qisqa so‘zlarga tarqatadi, shuning uchun gapning grammatikasini emas, musiqasini tinglang.

scenes.title: Soxta do‘st: actually
scenes.say: Actually signals a correction or a surprise: actually, I’ve already eaten. If you want to say that a topic is current and important, the word is topical.
scenes.say_native: Rus tilini biladiganlar uchun xavfli soxta do‘st: “actually”. U “актуально”, ya’ni dolzarb degani emas. “Actually” “aslida, haqiqatan” degani va ko‘pincha kutilmagan yoki to‘g‘rilovchi ma’lumotdan oldin keladi. Dolzarb mavzu inglizchada “a topical issue” yoki “a relevant issue”. Tinglashda “actually” eshitsangiz, so‘zlovchi oldingi fikrni tuzatmoqchi ekanini kuting.
scenes.say_uz: Actually tuzatish yoki kutilmagan ma’lumotni bildiradi: aslida men allaqachon ovqatlandim. Mavzu dolzarb va muhim demoqchi bo‘lsangiz, topical so‘zi kerak.

scenes.title: Munosabatni aniqlang
board: 1 Apparently, the new boss is very strict.
2 Surely you’re not wearing that to the interview?
3 To be fair, he did apologise.
4 Frankly, the second half was a waste of time.
scenes.say: Identify the attitude. One: Apparently, the new boss is very strict. Two: Surely you’re not wearing that to the interview? Three: To be fair, he did apologise. Four: Frankly, the second half was a waste of time.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Har birida so‘zlovchining munosabatini aniqlang: shubha, hayrat va norozilik, yon berish yoki ochiq tanqid. Kalit so‘zni toping va u nima uchun shu munosabatni bildirishini tushuntiring. Har bir gapni ichingizda ohang bilan o‘qib ko‘ring. Javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Munosabatni aniqlang. Bir: Aytishlaricha, yangi boshliq juda qattiqqo‘l. Ikki: Nahotki suhbatga shuni kiyib borasan? Uch: Insof bilan aytganda, u kechirim so‘radi. To‘rt: Ochig‘i, ikkinchi yarmi vaqtni behuda sarflash edi.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say: Notice the emphatic did in he did apologise: it insists on the fact, as if someone had just suggested the opposite.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “apparently” eshitilgan, tasdiqlanmagan ma’lumot. Ikkinchi: “surely” savolda hayrat va norozilik: “bu kiyim yaramaydi”. Uchinchi: “to be fair” yon berish, “did” esa urg‘u beradi: “u haqiqatan kechirim so‘radi”. To‘rtinchi: “frankly” ochiq tanqidni e’lon qiladi. Ikkinchidagi “surely” ni eslab qoling.
scenes.say_uz: He did apologise dagi urg‘uli did ga e’tibor bering: u faktni ta’kidlaydi, go‘yo kimdir hozirgina teskarisini aytgandek.

scenes.title: Kinoya va piching
board: Irony: saying the opposite of what you mean
Clues: context clash, stretched stress, flat tone
scenes.say: Irony works because the words clash with the situation. If someone says oh, brilliant as the printer jams for the third time, the context does all the work.
scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: hazil va kinoya. Kinoya, ya’ni “irony”, aytilgan gapning teskarisini nazarda tutish. Yomg‘ir quyib turganda “Lovely weather!” yoki ish buzilganda “Oh, brilliant”. Achchiqrog‘i “sarcasm”, piching. Uchta ishorani qidiring: gap vaziyatga zid bo‘ladi, urg‘u cho‘zilgan yoki bo‘rttirilgan bo‘ladi, yoki aksincha, ohang butunlay tekis.
scenes.say_uz: Kinoya so‘zlar vaziyatga zid kelgani uchun ishlaydi. Printer uchinchi marta tiqilib qolganda kimdir oh, ajoyib desa, butun ishni kontekst bajaradi.

scenes.title: Kamaytirib aytish
board: a bit of a problem (= a serious problem)
not the world’s greatest cook (= a terrible cook)

examples.t: We’ve had a bit of a problem with the roof.
examples.uz: Tom bilan ozgina muammo chiqdi. (aslida jiddiy)

scenes.say: Understatement is irony turned down to a whisper. The calmer the words, the bigger the disaster tends to be.
scenes.say_native: Britaniyaliklarning sevimli usuli kamaytirib aytish, ya’ni “understatement”. Tom qulab tushsa ham “a bit of a problem” deyishi mumkin. “Not ideal” ko‘pincha “yomon” degani. O‘zini kamsitib hazil qilish ham keng tarqalgan: “I’m not the world’s greatest cook” aslida “men yomon pishiraman”. Bu kamtarlik va hazilning aralashmasi, so‘zma-so‘z olmang.
scenes.say_uz: Kamaytirib aytish pichirlab aytilgan kinoya. So‘zlar qanchalik xotirjam bo‘lsa, falokat odatda shunchalik katta bo‘ladi.

scenes.title: Hazil va do‘stona mutoyiba
board: Deadpan: joke told with a straight face

examples.t: Nice of you to join us. (to a late friend, smiling)
examples.uz: Bizga qo‘shilganingiz uchun rahmat. (kechikkan do‘stga, kulib)

scenes.say: In British banter, teasing someone is often a sign of affection. If your colleagues never make fun of you, that may be the moment to worry.
scenes.say_native: Ingliz hazilining yana ikki turi bor. “Banter” do‘stlar orasidagi bir-birini masxara qilish, unda haqorat yo‘q, aksincha, yaqinlik belgisi. “Deadpan” esa hazilni mutlaqo jiddiy yuz va ovoz bilan aytish. O‘zbek askiyasi va Afandi latifalaridagi so‘z o‘yini sizga tanish, lekin o‘zbek hazilida kulgi odatda ochiqroq belgilanadi. Inglizcha deadpan hazilda belgi deyarli yo‘q.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniya mutoyibasida kimnidir masxara qilish ko‘pincha mehr belgisi. Hamkasblaringiz sizni hech qachon hazilga olmasa, aynan o‘shanda xavotirlanish kerak.

scenes.title: Kinoyaga jiddiy javob
board: ✗ B: Yes, I love meetings too!
✓ B: I know. Third one today.
scenes.say: Missing irony is not a grammar mistake, but it can be a social one. Respond to the attitude, not to the literal words.
scenes.say_native: Ko‘p uchraydigan holat: kinoyaga jiddiy javob berish. Hamkasbingiz charchagan ovozda “Oh great, another meeting” desa, u majlisni yoqtirmayotganini bildiryapti. “Yes, I love meetings too!” desangiz, kulgili vaziyat chiqadi. To‘g‘ri javob uning munosabatiga qo‘shilish: “I know. Third one today.” Kinoyani payqash muloqotda ham, imtihonda ham muhim.
scenes.say_uz: Kinoyani payqamaslik grammatik xato emas, lekin ijtimoiy xato bo‘lishi mumkin. Tom ma’noli so‘zlarga emas, munosabatga javob bering.

scenes.title: Samimiymi yoki kinoyami?
board: 1 (after a 3-hour delay) Well, that was quick.
2 (opening a gift) Oh, it’s lovely, thank you!
4 (roof collapsed) It’s not ideal, I admit.
scenes.say: Sincere, ironic or understated? One: after a three-hour delay, well, that was quick. Two: opening a gift, oh, it’s lovely, thank you! Three: the car won’t start, perfect, just perfect. Four: the roof has collapsed, it’s not ideal, I admit.
scenes.say_native: To‘rt vaziyat, qavs ichida kontekst berilgan. Har birida gap samimiymi, kinoyami yoki kamaytirib aytishmi, aniqlang. So‘zlarni emas, vaziyat bilan so‘z o‘rtasidagi ziddiyatni qidiring. Bitta holat samimiy bo‘lishi mumkin, uni toping. Har bir javobingizni qisqa sabab bilan asoslang.
scenes.say_uz: Samimiy, kinoya yoki kamaytirib aytishmi? Bir: uch soatlik kechikishdan keyin, xo‘sh, tez bo‘ldi. Ikki: sovg‘ani ochib, voy, chiroyli ekan, rahmat! Uch: mashina o‘t olmayapti, zo‘r, juda zo‘r. To‘rt: tom qulagan, ideal emas, tan olaman.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say: Without a clash between words and situation, assume sincerity. Irony needs a reason; if you cannot find one, take the words at face value.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: kinoya, chunki uch soatlik kechikish “tez” emas. Ikkinchi: ehtimol samimiy, chunki vaziyatda ziddiyat yo‘q, garchi ohang buni o‘zgartirishi mumkin. Uchinchi: kinoya, takrorlangan “perfect” norozilikni kuchaytiradi. To‘rtinchi: kamaytirib aytish, tom qulashi “not ideal” dan ancha jiddiy. Ikkinchida ohang hal qiluvchi ekaniga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say_uz: So‘z va vaziyat o‘rtasida ziddiyat bo‘lmasa, samimiy deb hisoblang. Kinoyaga sabab kerak; sabab topa olmasangiz, so‘zlarni tom ma’noda qabul qiling.

scenes.title: Tez nutq: qisqargan shakllar
board: don’t know → dunno · let me → lemme

examples.t: What do you want to do? → /ˈwɒdʒə ˈwɒnə ˈduː/

scenes.say: These reduced forms are not slang mistakes; they are how the words naturally sound at speed. You need to recognise them, even if you never write them.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: tez, tabiiy nutq. Ona tilida so‘zlashuvchilar urg‘usiz so‘zlarni qisqartiradi. “Going to” “gonna” ga, “want to” “wanna” ga, “don’t know” “dunno” ga aylanadi. “What do you want to do?” deyarli “wodja wanna do” kabi eshitiladi. Bular xato emas, tabiiy talaffuz. Yozuvda esa rasmiy matnda ishlatilmaydi, faqat tanish og‘zaki muloqotda.
scenes.say_uz: Bu qisqargan shakllar jargon xatosi emas, so‘zlar tez aytilganda tabiiy shunday eshitiladi. Ularni yozmasangiz ham, tanishingiz kerak.

scenes.title: Bog‘lanish va tushib qolish
board: Elision: next day /neks ˈdeɪ/ · last night /lɑːs ˈnaɪt/
scenes.say: Word boundaries disappear in fast speech. If you listen for separate words, you will hear a stream; listen instead for stressed syllables, and the rest falls into place.
scenes.say_native: Tez nutqda so‘zlar bir-biriga ulanadi. Undosh bilan tugagan so‘z unli bilan boshlangan so‘zga yopishadi: “turn it off” bitta so‘zdek eshitiladi. Britaniya talaffuzida odatda aytilmaydigan “r” keyingi unli oldida paydo bo‘ladi: “far away”. Ikki undosh orasida “t” va “d” ko‘pincha tushib qoladi: “next day” “neks day”, “last night” “las night” kabi eshitiladi.
scenes.say_uz: Tez nutqda so‘z chegaralari yo‘qoladi. Alohida so‘zlarni kutsangiz, faqat oqim eshitasiz; urg‘uli bo‘g‘inlarni tinglang, qolgani o‘z joyiga tushadi.

scenes.title: Britaniya va Amerika farqi
board: AmE: water, better → t sounds like a quick d
BrE (casual): not a lot → glottal stop [nɒʔ ə lɒʔ]
AmE gotta / BrE got to — both common
scenes.say: American speakers tend to soften t between vowels, while many British speakers replace it with a glottal stop. Both are normal, and both can make familiar words hard to recognise.
scenes.say_native: Ikki variantda tez nutq biroz farq qiladi. Amerika talaffuzida unlilar orasidagi “t” tez “d” ga o‘xshab qoladi: “water”, “better”. Britaniyaning norasmiy nutqida esa “t” o‘rniga ko‘pincha bo‘g‘iz to‘xtalishi eshitiladi: “not a lot” da “t” deyarli yo‘qoladi. Ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri, faqat tinglaganda tanib olish kerak. Darsliklardagi aniq talaffuz bilan adashib qolmang.
scenes.say_uz: Amerikaliklar unlilar orasidagi t ni yumshatadi, ko‘plab britaniyaliklar esa uni bo‘g‘iz to‘xtalishi bilan almashtiradi. Ikkalasi ham odatiy va ikkalasi ham tanish so‘zlarni tanib olishni qiyinlashtiradi.

scenes.title: Tez nutqni tinglash strategiyasi
board: 4 Shadow: repeat just behind the speaker
scenes.say: Shadowing trains your ear by forcing your mouth to keep up. Five minutes a day with a podcast is enough to notice a difference within a few weeks.
scenes.say_native: Tez nutq uchun strategiya. Birinchi: urg‘uli mazmunli so‘zlarni ushlang, ular ma’noning asosi. Ikkinchi: “actually”, “to be fair” kabi belgilardan yo‘l ko‘rsatkich sifatida foydalaning. Uchinchi: kontekstdan keyingi gapni taxmin qiling. To‘rtinchi, mashq uchun “shadowing”: audio ortidan yarim soniya kechikib, xuddi o‘sha ohangda takrorlang. Bu quloq va tilni birga mashq qildiradi.
scenes.say_uz: Shadowing og‘zingizni ortda qolmaslikka majburlab, qulog‘ingizni mashq qildiradi. Podkast bilan kuniga besh daqiqa bir necha haftada farqni sezishga yetadi.

scenes.title: Har bir so‘zni ushlashga urinish
board: ✗ Translate word by word in your head
scenes.say: If you miss a word, let it go. The next sentence will often explain it, and the speaker’s tone will tell you more than any single word could.
scenes.say_native: Eng katta xato: har bir so‘zni tushunishga urinish. Notanish so‘zda to‘xtab qolsangiz, keyingi uch gapni o‘tkazib yuborasiz. Ichingizda so‘zma-so‘z tarjima qilish ham sekinlashtiradi. Oqim bilan boring: so‘zlovchi kim, nimani istaydi, qanday munosabatda, shuni ushlang. Ko‘pincha keyingi gap notanish so‘zning ma’nosini o‘zi ochib beradi.
scenes.say_uz: Biror so‘zni o‘tkazib yuborsangiz, qo‘yib yuboring. Keyingi gap ko‘pincha uni tushuntiradi, so‘zlovchining ohangi esa bitta so‘zdan ko‘ra ko‘proq narsani aytadi.

scenes.title: Qisqargan shakllarni oching
board: 2 I dunno, we shoulda left earlier.
scenes.say: Expand each phrase into its full form. One: Whaddya reckon? Two: I dunno, we shoulda left earlier. Three: Gimme a sec. Four: Wanna grab a bite?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta qisqargan iboralar yozuvda ham ko‘rsatilgan. Har birini to‘liq, standart shaklda ayting. Avval ovoz chiqarib o‘qing va qaysi tovushlar birlashganini eshitishga harakat qiling. “Shoulda” ga ayniqsa e’tibor bering: oldingi darsdagi “should of” xatosini eslang.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir iborani to‘liq shaklga keltiring. Bir: Nima deb o‘ylaysan? Ikki: Bilmadim, ertaroq chiqishimiz kerak edi. Uch: Bir soniya bering. To‘rt: Biror narsa yeb olamizmi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 2 I don’t know, we should have left earlier.
4 Do you want to grab a bite?
scenes.say: In wanna grab a bite, the auxiliary do you has vanished completely. Fast questions often lose their opening words, so rely on rising intonation to recognise them as questions.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “What do you reckon?”, “reckon” britaniyacha “o‘ylamoq”. Ikkinchi: “I don’t know, we should have left earlier”, “shoulda” bu “should have”, “of” emas. Uchinchi: “Give me a second”. To‘rtinchi: “Do you want to grab a bite?”, boshidagi “do you” butunlay tushib qolgan. “Grab a bite” tez ovqatlanib olish degani.
scenes.say_uz: Wanna grab a bite da do you yordamchisi butunlay yo‘qolgan. Tez savollar ko‘pincha bosh so‘zlarini yo‘qotadi, shuning uchun ularni ko‘tariluvchi ohangdan taniysiz.

scenes.title: Dialog: ofisda
board: Manager: Nice to finally see it.
scenes.say: Manager: Ah, Dilnoza. Thanks for the report. Nice to finally see it. Dilnoza: Sorry, it took a bit longer than expected. Manager: So I gathered. Anyway, it’s, er, quite thorough. Forty pages, wasn’t it? Dilnoza: Forty-two. Manager: Right. I’ll save it for my weekend reading, then. Could we perhaps have a one-page summary by Friday?
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialogni tinglang. Rahbar Dilnozaning hisobotini oldi. Rahbar bironta ham qo‘pol so‘z aytmaydi, lekin u mamnun emas. Uning har bir gapida qanday yashirin ma’no borligini kuzating: “finally”, “So I gathered” va “quite thorough” ga alohida quloq soling. Dialogdan keyin uchta savol beraman.
scenes.say_uz: Rahbar: A, Dilnoza. Hisobot uchun rahmat. Nihoyat ko‘rganimdan xursandman. Dilnoza: Kechirasiz, kutilganidan biroz uzoqroq vaqt oldi. Rahbar: Shunday deb taxmin qilgandim. Xullas, u, mm, ancha batafsil. Qirq bet edi, shundaymi? Dilnoza: Qirq ikki. Rahbar: Tushunarli. Unda dam olish kunlari o‘qishga qoldiraman. Juma kunigacha bir betlik qisqacha mazmun olsak bo‘ladimi?

scenes.title: Tushunganingizni tekshiring
board: 1 Was the report on time? How do you know?
2 What does ‘quite thorough… forty pages’ imply?
3 What does the manager actually want?
scenes.say: One: was the report on time, and how do you know? Two: what does quite thorough, forty pages imply? Three: what does the manager actually want?
scenes.say_native: Dialog bo‘yicha uchta savol. Birinchi: hisobot o‘z vaqtida topshirildimi va buni qaysi so‘zlardan bilasiz? Ikkinchi: “quite thorough” va “forty pages” birga nimani anglatadi? Uchinchi: rahbar aslida nimani istaydi? Dam olish kunlari o‘qish haqidagi gap samimiymi yoki kinoyami, buni ham o‘ylang.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: hisobot o‘z vaqtida topshirildimi va buni qanday bilasiz? Ikki: ancha batafsil, qirq bet nimaga ishora qiladi? Uch: rahbar aslida nimani istaydi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say: The manager never says the report is late or too long, yet both messages are unmistakable. That is British workplace criticism in its purest form.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: yo‘q, kechikkan. “Finally” va “So I gathered”, ya’ni “buni sezdim”, kechikishga muloyim kinoya. Ikkinchi: “quite thorough”, “er” bilan ikkilanish va betlar soni hisobot haddan tashqari uzunligini bildiradi. Uchinchi: rahbarga bir betlik qisqacha mazmun kerak. Dam olish kunlari o‘qish haqidagi gap kinoya: u qirq ikki betni o‘qimoqchi emas.
scenes.say_uz: Rahbar hisobot kechikkan yoki juda uzun deb hech qachon aytmaydi, lekin ikkala xabar ham aniq. Bu Britaniya ish muhitidagi tanqidning eng sof ko‘rinishi.

scenes.title: Dialog: do‘stlar
board: Mind you, the views were stunning…
scenes.say: Sardor: So how was the camping trip? Kate: Oh, fantastic. It rained for three days, the tent leaked and Tom forgot the food. Sardor: Sounds idyllic. Kate: Honestly, it wasn’t ideal. Mind you, the views were stunning, when we could actually see them. Sardor: Going again next year? Kate: I dunno. Ask me when I’ve dried out.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog do‘stona va tezroq. Sardor dugonasi Keytdan sayohat qanday o‘tganini so‘raydi. Bu yerda ikki tomon ham kinoya qiladi va bu ularning yaqinligini ko‘rsatadi. Keyt nimani rost aytayotganini va nimani teskari ma’noda aytayotganini ajratishga harakat qiling.
scenes.say_uz: Sardor: Xo‘sh, chodirli sayohat qanday o‘tdi? Keyt: Voy, ajoyib. Uch kun yomg‘ir yog‘di, chodir chakka o‘tkazdi, Tom esa ovqatni unutib qoldirdi. Sardor: Jannatday ekan. Keyt: Rostini aytsam, ideal emas edi. Lekin manzaralar hayratlanarli edi, qachonki ularni ko‘ra olganimizda. Sardor: Kelasi yil yana borasanmi? Keyt: Bilmadim. Quriganimdan keyin so‘ra.

scenes.title: Tushunganingizni tekshiring
board: 2 What is Sardor doing with ‘Sounds idyllic’?
scenes.say: One: was the trip fantastic? Two: what is Sardor doing when he says sounds idyllic? Three: what was genuinely good? Four: will Kate go again?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Birinchi: sayohat haqiqatan ajoyib bo‘ldimi? Ikkinchi: Sardor “Sounds idyllic” deganda nima qilyapti? Uchinchi: sayohatda haqiqatan yaxshi narsa nima edi? To‘rtinchi: Keyt kelasi yil yana boradimi? Oxirgi javobda hazil borligini ham payqashga harakat qiling.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: sayohat ajoyib bo‘ldimi? Ikki: Sardor jannatday ekan deganda nima qilyapti? Uch: haqiqatan nima yaxshi edi? To‘rt: Keyt yana boradimi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say: Mind you introduces a qualification, often a positive point after a complaint. And it wasn’t ideal is classic understatement for three days of rain.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: yo‘q, “fantastic” kinoya, keyingi sanalgan muammolar buni isbotlaydi. Ikkinchi: Sardor ham kinoya bilan javob beradi, ya’ni hazilga qo‘shiladi, bu banter. Uchinchi: haqiqatan yaxshi narsa manzaralar, “mind you” cheklov kiritadi. To‘rtinchi: u hal qilmagan, “Ask me when I’ve dried out” hazil, lekin bunda ikkilanish ham bor.
scenes.say_uz: Mind you cheklov kiritadi, ko‘pincha shikoyatdan keyin ijobiy nuqtani. It wasn’t ideal esa uch kunlik yomg‘ir uchun klassik kamaytirib aytish.

scenes.title: To‘rt qisqa parcha
scenes.say: Clip one: I’d love to, but I’ve got a lot on this week. Clip two: You might want to double-check those figures before the meeting. Clip three: Well, that’s certainly one way of doing it. Clip four: If I were you, I’d grab a ticket now. They won’t last.
scenes.say_native: Endi to‘rtta juda qisqa parchani tinglang. Har birida so‘zlovchining maqsadi bor: rad etish, ogohlantirish, norozilik yoki maslahat. Maqsad hech qayerda ochiq aytilmaydi, uni so‘z tanlovi va tuzilmadan topasiz. Bu xuddi uy vazifangizdagi mashqning o‘zi.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi parcha: Juda xohlardim, lekin bu hafta ishim ko‘p. Ikkinchi parcha: Majlisdan oldin o‘sha raqamlarni yana bir tekshirib chiqsangiz yaxshi bo‘lardi. Uchinchi parcha: Xo‘sh, bu ham bir usul, albatta. To‘rtinchi parcha: Men sizning o‘rningizda hozir chipta olardim. Tez tugaydi.

scenes.title: Maqsadni toping
scenes.say: Match each clip to an intention: refusing, warning, disapproving or advising. Then name the phrase that gave it away.
scenes.say_native: Har bir parchaga maqsadni moslang: rad etish, ogohlantirish, norozilik yoki maslahat. Har biri uchun dalilni ham ayting: qaysi ibora maqsadni ochib berdi? Masalan, “I’d love to, but” qanday ishlaydi? Nima uchun inglizlar “no” demasdan rad etadi, shuni ham o‘ylang. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir parchani maqsadga moslang: rad etish, ogohlantirish, norozilik yoki maslahat. Keyin buni ochib bergan iborani ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 3 Disapproving: one way of doing it
scenes.say: You might want to sounds optional, but it is usually an instruction or a warning. When a manager says it, treat it as urgent.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: rad etish, “I’d love to, but” klassik muloyim rad. Ikkinchi: ogohlantirish, “You might want to” yumshoq ko‘rinadi, lekin aslida “raqamlarda xato bor” degani. Uchinchi: norozilik, “one way of doing it” bu usul noto‘g‘ri ekaniga ishora. To‘rtinchi: maslahat, “If I were you” va “They won’t last” tezlashtiradi.
scenes.say_uz: You might want to ixtiyoriy eshitiladi, lekin odatda bu ko‘rsatma yoki ogohlantirish. Rahbar shunday desa, uni shoshilinch deb qabul qiling.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq
board: A Refuse indirectly (3 ways): Can you work this Saturday?
B Say ‘Great, thanks.’ sincerely, then ironically
C Use: I’d love to, but… / I’m afraid… / tricky
scenes.say: Your turn. First, refuse this request in three indirect ways without saying no: can you work this Saturday? Then say great, thanks, once sincerely and once ironically.
scenes.say_native: Endi o‘zingiz gapirasiz. Birinchi: “Can you work this Saturday?” savoliga uchta turli bilvosita rad javobini ayting, birortasida ham “no” so‘zi bo‘lmasin. Ikkinchi: “Great, thanks” iborasini avval samimiy, keyin kinoya bilan ayting. Ohang farqini o‘zingiz eshiting. Ovozingizni yozib olsangiz, yanada yaxshi.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizda. Avval bu iltimosni no demasdan uch xil bilvosita rad eting: shu shanba ishlay olasizmi? Keyin great, thanks ni bir marta samimiy, bir marta kinoya bilan ayting.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javoblar
board: I’d really like to help, but I’ve already made plans.
Saturday’s a bit tricky for me, I’m afraid.
Let me check, but I don’t think I can.
scenes.say: I’d really like to help, but I’ve already made plans. Saturday’s a bit tricky for me, I’m afraid. Let me check, but I don’t think I can. And listen: great, thanks! Now: grreat. Thanks.
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javoblarni tinglang. Uchalasida ham “no” yo‘q, lekin ma’no aniq. Kinoyali “Great, thanks” da birinchi so‘z cho‘zilgan va ohang tekis yoki pasaygan bo‘ladi. Samimiysida esa ovoz yuqoridan jonli tushadi. O‘zingiznikini solishtiring: rad javobingizda sabab yoki afsus bormi, ohangingiz farq qildimi?
scenes.say_uz: Yordam berishni juda xohlardim, lekin rejalarim bor. Shanba men uchun biroz noqulay, afsuski. Tekshirib ko‘ray, lekin qila olmasam kerak. Endi tinglang: ajoyib, rahmat! Endi esa: ajoyib. Rahmat.

scenes.title: Takrorlash
board: Implied meaning: what is not said
Markers: well, actually, to be fair, frankly
Fast speech: reductions, linking, stressed words
scenes.say: Listen for what is missing, notice the markers, check the words against the situation and follow the stressed syllables. That is how you hear intention, not just words.
scenes.say_native: Qisqacha takrorlaymiz. Yashirin ma’no ko‘pincha aytilmagan narsada. Munosabat belgilari va ravishlar keyingi gapni e’lon qiladi. Ohang, ayniqsa pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang, aytilmagan “lekin” ni bildiradi. Kinoya so‘z va vaziyat ziddiyatidan tug‘iladi, kamaytirib aytish esa uning yumshoq ko‘rinishi. Tez nutqda urg‘uli so‘zlarni ushlang va qisqargan shakllarni taning.
scenes.say_uz: Yo‘q narsani tinglang, belgilarni payqang, so‘zlarni vaziyat bilan solishtiring va urg‘uli bo‘g‘inlarga ergashing. Shunda faqat so‘zlarni emas, niyatni eshitasiz.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Write out 1 reduced form in full
scenes.say: Your homework: find five short authentic clips and identify the speaker’s intention in each, with evidence. Next time we explore cultural context and historical references.
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: besh qisqa haqiqiy parcha toping, podkast, serial yoki intervyudan. Har biri uchun so‘zlovchining niyatini bir so‘z bilan yozing va dalilini qayd eting: belgi, ohang, kamaytirib aytish yoki kontekst. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: beshtadan kamida to‘rttasida niyat va dalil aniq bo‘lsin, har biridan bitta qisqargan shaklni to‘liq yozing. Keyingi darsda madaniy kontekst va tarixiy ishoralarni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifangiz: besh qisqa haqiqiy parcha topib, har birida so‘zlovchi niyatini dalili bilan aniqlang. Keyingi safar madaniy kontekst va tarixiy ishoralarni o‘rganamiz.

homework_uz: Ingliz tilidagi besh qisqa audio yoki video parcha tanlang (podkast, serial, intervyu, har biri 30 soniyagacha). Har biri uchun so‘zlovchining niyatini bir so‘z bilan yozing (masalan, rad etish, tanqid, maqtov, kinoya, maslahat) va buni qaysi dalil ko‘rsatganini qayd eting: munosabat belgisi, ohang, kamaytirib aytish yoki kontekst. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: beshtadan kamida to‘rttasida niyat va dalil aniq yozilgan bo‘lsin, har bir parchadan kamida bitta qisqargan shaklni to‘liq shaklda yozing.

quiz.q: A: ‘Is the report ready?’ B: ‘I’ve been in meetings all day.’ What does B mean?
quiz.why_uz: Bilvosita javob: sabab aytiladi, ma’nosi esa yo‘q.

quiz.q: In British English, what does ‘I hear what you say’ usually signal?
quiz.why_uz: Bu muloyim ibora odatda qo‘shilmaslikni bildiradi.

quiz.q: Which marker most often introduces criticism?
quiz.why_uz: Frankly ochiq fikr, ko‘pincha tanqid oldidan keladi.
Actually = aslida; dolzarb ma’nosi yo‘q, bu rus tilidagi актуально bilan soxta do‘st.

quiz.q: A friend says ‘Oh, brilliant’ when the train is cancelled. This is …
‘We’ve had a bit of a problem with the roof’ (the roof collapsed). This is …
What is the full form of ‘I dunno’?
quiz.why_uz: Dunno — don’t know ning tez nutqdagi qisqargan shakli.

quiz.q: ‘You might want to double-check those figures.’ What is the intention?
options: A warning that something is wrong
quiz.why_uz: Yumshoq shaklda, lekin aslida raqamlarda xato borligi haqida ogohlantirish.

quiz.q: What does a fall-rise tone on ‘The food was good’ suggest?
quiz.why_uz: Pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang aytilmagan lekin ga ishora qiladi.

quiz.q: What is the best strategy when you miss a word in fast speech?
options: Keep listening for stressed words and context
Ask the speaker to spell it
quiz.why_uz: Oqim bilan boring; keyingi gap va kontekst ko‘pincha ma’noni ochadi.
